questions.text: Do you work, or are you a student?
questions.say: Good afternoon. My name is Emma, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about what you do. Do you work, or are you a student?

questions.text: What would you change about your work or studies if you could?
questions.say: What would you change about your work or studies if you could?

questions.text: Is there a skill you need to improve for your work or studies?
questions.say: Is there a skill you need to improve for your work or studies?

questions.text: What is a normal working or study day like for you?
questions.say: What is a normal working or study day like for you?

questions.text: Do you write much by hand these days?
questions.say: Now let's move on to talk about writing. Do you write much by hand these days?

questions.text: What kind of things do you write?
questions.say: What kind of things do you write?

questions.text: Did you like writing stories as a child?
questions.say: Did you like writing stories as a child?

questions.text: Do you ever take a nap during the day?
questions.say: Now let's move on to talk about naps. Do you ever take a nap during the day?

questions.text: Where do you usually take a nap?
questions.say: Where do you usually take a nap?

questions.text: Do you feel better after a short sleep in the afternoon?
questions.say: Do you feel better after a short sleep in the afternoon?

cueCard.topic: Describe a time when you worked in a team.
points: what the team had to do
cueCard.explain: and explain how you felt about working in this team.

questions.text: Describe a time when you worked in a team.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe a time when you worked in a team. You should say: what the team had to do; who was in the team; what your role was; and explain how you felt about working in this team.

questions.text: Would you like to work with the same people again?
questions.say: Thank you. Would you like to work with the same people again?

questions.text: Why do teachers often ask students to work in groups?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about a time when you worked in a team, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all teamwork at school. Why do teachers often ask students to work in groups?

questions.text: What problems can happen when students work in a group?
questions.say: What problems can happen when students work in a group?

questions.text: Is it better for children to learn in teams or on their own?
questions.say: Is it better for children to learn in teams or on their own?

questions.text: What makes a team successful at work?
questions.say: Now let's talk about teamwork at work. What makes a team successful at work?

questions.text: Is it important for colleagues to be friends?
questions.say: Is it important for colleagues to be friends?

questions.text: Do you think people will work in teams more or less in the future?
questions.say: Do you think people will work in teams more or less in the future?
